### W17.18 · Fix: the tests that check a SIGKILLed hangup-ignoring child right after `close_all` fail on a loaded run
Parent: W17.7
Status: confirmed
Approach: Three tests in scripts/test_ptyrelay.py fail intermittently: `Ending.test_quitting_the_screen_leaves_no_hangup_ignoring_child_behind`, `IdleEnds.test_quitting_just_after_the_idle_close_still_kills_a_hangup_ignoring_child` and `IdleEnds.test_quitting_just_after_new_chat_still_kills_a_hangup_ignoring_child`. Running `python3 -m unittest test_ptyrelay` four times failed three of the four (a different one of these each time, "the SIGKILL step ... was lost at exit" / "the child was still running when close_all returned"); each alone passes most runs (IdleEnds alone failed 1 in 5 and 1 in 8). The cause: `Relay.close`'s reaper returns as soon as `os.killpg(pid, SIGKILL)` returns, but the kernel kills the processes a moment later (a loop polling /proc right after `close_all` saw the child still alive for about 1 ms in some runs), and each test then calls `alive()` once with no wait. So the tests give a false failure, and `ChatHost.close_all`'s docstring ("returns only when each is gone") and the W17.7 claim that the child "is gone when the screen quits" are stronger than what the code guarantees. Settle it by making the code keep its word: in `Relay.close`'s `reap`, after the SIGKILL, wait a bounded time (about 1 s, polling `_group_exists`, treating a still-listed zombie as gone as the tests do) for the group to empty, so `close_all` returns with the group dead; and/or have the three tests poll with `until(lambda: not alive(), 2)`. Done when `python3 -m unittest test_ptyrelay` passes ten runs in a row and the three tests still fail with `reap`'s SIGKILL removed.

### W17.19 · Hypothesis: every process a chat's agent starts stays in the agent's process group
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: W17.1 (and W17.7, W17.14, W17.17 that build on it) assume that everything the agent starts is in the process group `pty.fork` made, so `os.killpg(pid, ...)` in `Relay.close` ends all of it and `_group_cpu` (keyed on the group id) sees all its cpu. A tool process, MCP server or background task that the agent starts with its own session or group (`setsid`, `detached: true` in node, `nohup setsid`) is in neither: closing the chat leaves it running, which is the leak the Goal is about, and its cpu use does not keep the chat from being idle. Nothing was run against a real claude, codex, kiro or opencode, and the node carries no Hypothesis. State it as a Hypothesis with its page (what would show it wrong: after a real agent chat that started a long tool process or background task is closed, by hand, by New chat or by the idle close, a process of it is still running; check with `ps -eo pid,pgid,sid,args` before and after), and add the evidence for or against it from a run or from the agent's own documentation, not from issue reports alone. If it is wrong, the follow-up is to also kill by session id or by walking descendants through /proc.
Hypothesis: Every process a chat's agent starts stays in the agent's process group, so `os.killpg` in `Relay.close` ends all of it and `_group_cpu` sees all its cpu. Wrong if, after a real agent chat that started a long tool process or background task is closed (by hand, by New chat or by the idle close), a process of it is still running; check with `ps -eo pid,pgid,sid,args` before and after. .dfs/artefacts/59789f89-429a-4bd5-9538-dc034e268b73.html
Evidence:
- for: a stub agent's plain background child (started with `&`) was gone after `Relay.close`, and a hangup-ignoring one after `close_all` (the W17.1 and W17.7 tests); scripts/run.sh execs the agent with no new session (read in W17.6). Stubs, not a real agent.
- against: a probe (bash agent on a `Relay`, `sleep 61 &` and `setsid sleep 62 &`, `ps -eo pid,pgid,sid,stat,args` after `Relay.close` and 3.5 s) showed the plain child gone and the setsid child still running in its own group and session. So a child that starts its own session escapes the close, and its cpu is invisible to the idle check.
- for: the claude-code issues found (#76306 Windows launcher chains, #33947 and #40550 MCP servers orphaned when claude is killed) describe MCP servers as ordinary children of claude, left behind when claude dies; none says they start their own session. Second-hand, none read for POSIX detach behaviour.
- not settled: no claude, codex, kiro or opencode is installed here, so whether any of them starts a tool with `detached: true` or `setsid` was not seen. If one does, the follow-up is to also kill by session id or walk the descendants through /proc.

Parent: W17.18
Status: confirmed
Approach: One line each:

### W17.21 · Fix: a chat whose agent exits by itself leaves its hangup-ignoring children running
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: `Relay.close` (scripts/ptyrelay.py) signals the group only `if self.live`, and `Relay._pump` sets `self.fd = None` once the pty reaches EOF and then reaps the agent with `os.waitpid`; nothing signals the group on that path. So when the agent ends on its own (the author types /exit after attaching, or it crashes) while something it started ignores hangup (`nohup`, a `trap '' HUP`) and does not hold the pty, the relay is "not live", `ChatHost.reap_idle` just drops it (`del self.relays[scope]`) and `close_all` skips it, and that child runs for ever: the leak the Goal is about. Reproduced: a `ChatHost.ensure` of `sh -c "trap '' HUP; (trap '' HUP; exec sleep 63 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1) & sleep 0.5; exit 0"`, then 2s: `live` False, `ps -eo pid,pgid,sid,stat,args` shows `sleep 63` still in the agent's group; `reap_idle()` returned [] and after `close_all()` plus 1.5s it was still running. (The kernel's hangup on the session leader's exit reaches only processes that do not ignore it.) Settle it by ending the group when the agent has exited: in `_pump`, after the pty EOF and before the agent is reaped (so its pid cannot have been reused; for instance `os.waitid(os.P_PID, pid, os.WEXITED | os.WNOWAIT)`, then `os.killpg(pid, SIGKILL)` guarded for ESRCH, then `os.waitpid`), kill the group with SIGKILL; the same for the pump ending because the pty closed with the agent still running is not needed, `close` handles it. Done when a new test in test_ptyrelay.py (the agent above, then `until(lambda: not alive(child), 3)`) fails without the change and passes with it, and `python3 -m unittest test_ptyrelay` still passes.

### W17.23 · Fix: on a Python without `os.waitid` the chat's pump thread dies on an AttributeError and never reaps the agent
Parent: W17.21
Status: open
Approach: W17.21 added `os.waitid(os.P_PID, self.pid, os.WEXITED | os.WNOWAIT)` to `Relay._pump` in scripts/ptyrelay.py, inside `try ... except ChildProcessError`. `os.waitid` does not exist on macOS before Python 3.13 (the Python docs for `os.waitid` say "Changed in version 3.13: This function is now available on macOS as well"; a saspy issue shows the AttributeError on a Mac). The repo supports darwin (flake.nix `systems` lists x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin) and README tells the author to run `python3 scripts/web.py` directly, so the system python3 may be an older one (the flake pins nixpkgs but a direct run does not use it). There the `AttributeError` is not caught: the pump thread dies after closing the pty and before `os.waitpid`, so every chat that ends leaves the agent a zombie, `rc` stays None, and the group is never killed (the leak W17.21 meant to close is open again, and the W17.21 test fails). Before W17.21 this worked on those Pythons. Settle it: guard the call (`hasattr(os, "waitid")`, or catch AttributeError) and, where it is missing, fall back to killing the group with `os.killpg(self.pid, SIGKILL)` just before `os.waitpid` (the agent is not yet reaped when waitpid has not run, so its pid cannot have been reused; the pty is already gone, so nothing else will signal it). Always reach the `os.waitpid` whatever the earlier step raises (put it in a `finally`). Done when a test in scripts/test_ptyrelay.py that patches `ptyrelay.os.waitid` away (for instance `mock.patch.object(ptyrelay.os, "waitid", side_effect=AttributeError)` or `delattr` under `mock.patch.dict`) still sees `relay.rc` set and the hangup-ignoring child of the W17.21 test gone, and that test fails with the guard removed; `python3 -m unittest test_ptyrelay` still passes.

### W17.24 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W17.21
Status: open
Approach: One line each:
- scripts/ptyrelay.py `_pump` now SIGKILLs the whole group the moment the agent exits, also in the middle of `Relay.close`, so a child that was hanging up gracefully after the SIGHUP (an MCP server flushing state) is cut off at once instead of getting GRACE; the `reap` comment ("Give the group GRACE seconds to go") and the module docstring no longer describe that. Say so, or kill in `_pump` only when `closing` is false.
- scripts/ptyrelay.py `_pump`: if the agent lets go of the pty but ignores hangup and keeps running, `waitid` blocks until it exits, the relay is not `live`, and `close`/`close_all` skip it, so it is not ended (the W17.21 Approach said `close` handles this; it does not). Unlikely for a real agent; the comment in `_pump` ("or let go of the pty") says more than the code does.
- scripts/ptyrelay.py: `_group_running` and `_group_cpu` parse /proc/<pid>/stat for every process on each call; fine for now, but nothing in the docstrings says they are Linux only (they return "nothing busy" elsewhere, so the 6-hour ceiling and cpu check silently do not apply on macOS).
- scripts/test_chat.py `test_it_will_not_send_while_the_screens_chat_is_open_on_the_session` fails here (65 tests, 1 failure) and on the base commit; not from this task.
